key_insight: A conditional flow-matching generative model can rapidly synthesize plausible 3D urban wind and temperature fields from building geometry and mean flow, capturing turbulent variability rather than only deterministic averages.
engineering_relevance: This enables near-real-time, turbulence-aware urban microclimate assessment for design iteration, local gust analysis, and climate-adaptation planning without repeated expensive LES runs.
method: Uses Conditional Flow Matching as a generative surrogate conditioned on urban geometry and mean flow.
Generates 3D instantaneous velocity and temperature fields in pixel space.
Mitigates GPU memory limits by running on overlapping subdomains with shared-noise initialization to preserve continuity.
evidence_signal: Compared with LES, the model reported low NRMSE for first-order statistics (2.99% wind, 1.77% temperature) and good agreement for turbulence metrics, TKE, PDFs, and vertical profiles.
watch_item: Pixel-space 3D generation with subdomain stitching may be sensitive to boundary consistency and memory constraints, so domain decomposition and continuity handling must be implemented carefully.
paper_title: Conditional Flow Matching for Generation of 3D Multi-variable Instantaneous Urban Microclimate Fields
